question: In which year did Eric A. Cornell, Wolfgang Ketterle and Carl E. Wieman receive the Nobel Prize in Physics for the achieving 'Bose-Einstein condensation in dilute gases of alkali atoms'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2001**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Eric A. Cornell, Wolfgang Ketterle, and Carl E. Wieman received the Nobel Prize in Physics in the year **2001**.
 
• They were awarded for achieving **'Bose-Einstein condensation in dilute gases of alkali atoms'**.
 
• Their work was instrumental in demonstrating a new state of matter predicted by Satyendra Nath Bose and Albert Einstein in the early 20th century.
 
• This achievement has significant implications in the field of quantum mechanics and has opened up new avenues for research in physics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Nobel Prize in Physics is awarded annually by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences.
 
• The prize recognizes outstanding contributions in the field of physics and has been awarded since 1901.
 
• Winners receive a medal, a diploma, and a cash award.
 
• The Nobel Prizes were established by the will of Alfred Nobel, the inventor of dynamite.
 
• Eric A. Cornell and Carl E. Wieman conducted their research at the University of Colorado, while Wolfgang Ketterle conducted his research at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT).
